decisions.reason: As a still-young safety-shoe line in the firm’s core business, it would usually be retained by a large established producer unless its results were clearly below aspiration levels.

The supportive insole still fits the product system, but after the earlier withdrawal of another insole and given possible overlap in the range, it faces the highest risk of being dropped if performance remains below aspirations.
The ergonomic safety-shoe series remains close to the core offer and the prior dedicated presentation suggests continued managerial commitment, so it is likely to be given more time.
Firefighter and rescue boots are a more specialized niche, so they stay if acceptable demand is visible but remain somewhat more exposed than core safety-shoe lines if results disappoint.

Because the moulded insole was positioned as a flagship direction, management would be very reluctant to withdraw it quickly and would usually continue backing it unless evidence of failure became strong.
